headline: Open tools for selection, admixture, and ancestry inference from genomic data
label: Population Genomics Software Tools
summary: Recent tools automate selection scans, admixture and ancestry estimation, and low-coverage simulation over large genomic datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the packaging of established population-genetic inference methods into faster, automated, or more accessible software. XPCLRS reimplements XP-CLR in Rust with native multithreading and is reported as up to hundreds of times faster. CAPHEINE automates exploratory HyPhy selection analyses from unaligned pathogen sequences and a reference genome. Mixtum and KANN estimate two-way admixture proportions and individual ancestry from biallelic genotypes and principal components, respectively, with KANN supporting continuous reference profiles. PyEvoMotion, SERAPHIM 2.0, and lcSimVCF extend time-course clock modeling, phylogeographic analysis, and low-coverage genotype likelihood simulation. These contributions differ in target problem and implementation, so the shared feature is workflow tooling rather than a common statistical representation.
